items.feature: Payload type: Custom iterator
items.gap: Implemented as a positional cartesian-product generator: IntruderGenerators::customIterator(positions, separator) emits every combination pos[0][i]+sep+pos[1][j]+... in odometer order (last position varies fastest), reachable via type "iterator" on /api/intruder/generate and /api/intruder/set. Matches Burp's core custom-iterator behaviour; the only nicety not carried is a DISTINCT separator per position (one shared between-positions separator instead) -- noted as a possible enhancement, not a gap that blocks the use case.
items.why: Implemented + mutation-proven, following the exact pattern the other 12 payload generators use (all marked present): a pure Qt6::Core-linkable IG function + expandGen dispatch + types() entry. Bounded at kMaxCount by capping the working set after EACH position, so a huge product truncates in COUNT while every emitted payload stays a COMPLETE combination (never a length-truncated fragment) and never OOMs.
items.evidence: intruder_generators.cpp:314 customIterator(); types() (:344) lists "iterator"; control_server.cpp:3648 expandGen `if (t == "iterator")` parses positions (arrays or newline-joined) + separator. Tests/intruder_generators/intruder_generators_test.cpp (107 pass): odometer order + separator, no-separator concat, single-position no-sep, 3-position join, empty/empty-factor -> empty, and 47^3 capped at kMaxCount with every payload complete; M1 (drop separator) + M2 (drop cap) each fail only their targeted case. reconciled.note: Closed 2026-08-12. NAME CORRECTED: the audit labelled this 'Character substring' with a 'progressive substrings' gap, but Burp Intruder has no 'substring' payload type -- its documented type is 'Character substitution' (leetspeak). Implemented that (the real Burp feature): IntruderGenerators::charSub(items, subs) emits, per item, all 2^k permutations of applying-or-not each substitutable character position (e.g. peter + {e:3,t:7} -> peter/p3ter/pe7er/p37er/pet3r/p3t3r/pe73r/p373r), enumerated leftmost-position-as-LSB to match Burp's order. Verified against the PortSwigger docs. Wired into control_server expandGen (t==charsub, items from array/newline, subs from a {char:char} object) + types(). Unit- + mutation-tested (linearising the 2^k enumeration fails the multi-position cases).

reconciled.note: Closed 2026-08-11: added IntruderGenerators::caseMod(items, modes) -- for each item, one payload per enabled case option in canonical order, item-major, no dedup. The FIVE Burp options confirmed from the PortSwigger docs (a vetting-agent 4-mode proposal was wrong): No change / lower / upper / Propername (first cp upper, rest LOWER) / ProperName (first cp upper, rest UNCHANGED). Distinct from the 1:1 intruder_rules uppercase/lowercase transforms -- this is a list-multiplying payload TYPE. First char upper-cased by code point (non-BMP safe). Wired into control_server expandGen (t==casemod, items from array/newline-split, modes from a token array defaulting to all five). Unit- + mutation-tested (collapsing Propername's lower-rest fails the lower-rest cases; the Propername vs ProperName distinction is the docs' 'critical difference').

items.feature: Payload type: Recursive grep
items.gap: No chaining an extracted value into the next request; blocks CSRF-token/nonce walking and stateful sequences.
items.why: Re-read the fire loop. computeGrep results are stored on the row and never fed forward into the next request's payload. Confirmed absent.
items.evidence: intruder.cpp:445-507 fireOne computes grep (484-487) and posts it to the row; combos are pre-generated at :376-378 before firing — no path takes a response-N extract into request N+1.

reconciled.note: ENGINE done (the hard part the audit called 'weeks'): the extract IS now fed forward. Recursive grep runs as a SERIAL branch in Intruder::runWorker -- each request's payload is the value the grep-EXTRACT spec pulls from the PREVIOUS response, walked from a `seed` for `count` requests, stopping early when a response yields no extract (chain ended). fireOne was refactored to RETURN its extracted value (it already computed it for the result column) and to record the runtime-discovered payload into the row; start() reserves `count` placeholder rows and forces concurrency 1 (the run is inherently serial -- each request depends on the prior response); it reuses the existing IntruderGrep::grepExtract spec as the payload source, so no new extraction code. Config via /api/intruder/set { recursiveGrep, recursiveGrepSeed, recursiveGrepCount }; snapshot exposes intruder.recursiveGrep. VERIFIED e2e against a chaining mock: a 5-request walk carried exactly [seed, TOK0, TOK1, TOK2, TOK3] (each request carried the PRIOR response's extracted token -- the chain proven), result rows recorded the extracted token + the payload used, `count` bounded the run, and a dried-up token stopped the chain early (fired 3 of 10). Gauntlet ctest 98/98 + probe_smoke 156/156. This is the classic anti-CSRF-bruteforce / one-time-nonce / state-machine walk. REMAINDER (-> stays partial): the ui-v2 payload-type selector + seed/count fields (concurrent-agent lane), save/resume (RunConfig) of a recursive attack, and multi-position recursive (only position 0 carries the recursive value today, Sniper-style).

items.feature: Processing rule: Add raw payload
items.gap: None -- add-raw-payload is a new local op in the processing-rule chain: it appends the ORIGINAL, pre-chain payload value regardless of what earlier rules already did to the running value, so e.g. [sha256] -> [add-raw-payload] yields "<hash><rawvalue>" for sign-then-send patterns.
items.why: Closed: applyRule/applyRules only ever saw the current running value, with no way to reach back to the pre-chain original once an earlier rule had transformed it. Gave applyRule a third `original` parameter (the 2-arg overload defaults it to `value` itself, preserving every existing call site and test) and had applyRules thread the constant pre-chain value through as `original` on every step, so add-raw-payload works correctly no matter where it sits in the chain or how many times it repeats.
items.evidence: Src/Core/Networking/intruder_rules.hpp:56-57 (applyRule 3-arg + 2-arg overloads), intruder_rules.cpp:28-35 (add-raw-payload op + original threading), :169-172 (applyRules passes the constant original), operations() now advertises add-raw-payload; ui-v2/tabs.jsx RULE_OPS_FALLBACK includes it (the live list already comes from GET /api/intruder/rule-ops -> IntruderRules::operations(), control_server.cpp:3635-3639); Tests/intruder_rules/intruder_rules_test.cpp adds 5 checks (standalone self-append, appends original past an earlier transform, sha256-then-raw sign-then-send pattern, repeated add-raw-payload chain, operations() advertisement).

reconciled.note: absent -> present. Burp Payload Processing rule "Add raw payload": re-inserts the unmodified original payload at that point in the chain, most commonly used after a hash/encode step to build a sign-then-send value (hash+raw). The engine (intruder_rules.cpp) previously threaded only the running value through each rule with no notion of the untouched pre-chain original, so there was no way to get back to it once an earlier rule (e.g. sha256) had overwritten the running value. Added a third `original` parameter to applyRule (2-arg overload defaults it to value, so every existing call site and the 40+ existing unit tests are untouched) and have applyRules thread the constant pre-chain payload through as `original` on every step of the loop, so add-raw-payload appends the true original no matter where it sits in the chain or how many times it repeats. items.feature: Rule action: "Check session is valid" (issue a validation request, match a keyword/status/redirect, and conditionally run the re-auth macro)
items.gap: No session-validity detection and no automatic re-authentication. A long Intruder run or audit scan that logs out midway produces a page of meaningless 302s with no warning — and given the Repeater/Intruder bypass above, those tools were never carrying the session anyway.
items.why: Confirmed. I read applyToRequest and applyToResponse in full: both are pure string manipulation with no network I/O and no conditional branch on response content.
items.evidence: session_rules.cpp:133-237 `SessionRules::applyToRequest` performs only template substitution into four targets and never constructs a request; :74-131 `applyToResponse` only harvests values into `m_varsByHost`. Neither includes networking.hpp. Greps for reauth / sessionInvalid / loggedOut / relogin / checkSession across Src/: 0 hits.

reconciled.note: Built: the session-validity check + conditional re-auth now exist. SessionRulesLogic::responseIsLoggedOut(status, bodyText, statusList, bodyRegex) (session_rules_logic.cpp:133-147) is a pure, unit-tested + mutation-proven predicate -- a comma status list (e.g. "401,403") and/or a response-body regex; BOTH empty = never (a macro with no condition never auto-re-auths); status 0 (no response) never matches; an invalid regex fails closed. A SessionMacro (session_rules.hpp:86-95) carries loggedOutStatus/loggedOutBodyRegex; SessionRules::maybeReauth, called from applyToResponse, matches every live response to the macro's sessionHost against it and on a hit re-runs the macro ASYNC (QtConcurrent::run -- never blocks the proxy worker on login I/O) to re-acquire the session, then ingests the fresh vars into the host bag. Loop-guarded: an in-flight QSet + a 5s per-host cooldown, and the macro's own requests use ChainRunner's client (not the proxy) so a permanently-failing login can't hammer the target or re-trigger itself. PARTIAL, honestly: this detects a logged-out session PASSIVELY on the live response stream rather than issuing Burp's dedicated active 'validation request' to a known URL, and there is still no in-browser recovery prompt; but the core -- match status/keyword and conditionally run the re-auth macro -- is real. Closes launch blocker #11 ("no check-session-is-valid").

items.feature: Container/Docker distribution for headless + CI
items.gap: The build-docker CI job (added last wave) is now confirmed GREEN end-to-end: `docker build` succeeds and `docker run ... --help` starts cleanly, closing the 'self-declared unvalidated, nothing ever proves it builds' half of the prior gap for real (last wave had only wired the job in without a Docker daemon to pre-validate it -- its very first real run failed, five times in a row, on real bugs this wave root-caused and fixed one at a time). Still genuinely missing: no published/pushed image (a `docker pull` still isn't possible -- the file only builds locally or in CI, it is not a distribution channel yet) and the base images are pinned to a version tag (`ubuntu:22.04`) rather than a content digest, so a tag repoint could still silently change the build.
items.why: Confirmed the build-docker job's first real run (commit 41710a4/e73e96a) had actually failed -- `conclusion: failure` on GitHub Actions, not yet checked at the time it was added. Root-caused and fixed five distinct real bugs, one CI round-trip (~15-20min each, no docker daemon in this cloud session to pre-validate any of them locally) at a time, all specific to a bare `ubuntu:22.04` container lacking things GitHub's hosted runner images ship pre-installed and CI's `jurplel/install-qt-action` (which the Dockerfile's raw `aqt install-qt` call approximates, not calls) papers over: (1) aqtinstall renamed the Linux desktop arch from `gcc_64` to `linux_gcc_64` as of Qt 6.7.0 -- the Dockerfile's pin to 6.7.3 needed the new name; (2) Ubuntu 22.04's apt cmake (3.22.1) is older than CMakeLists.txt's `cmake_minimum_required(3.24)` -- switched to installing cmake via pip; (3) `zlib1g-dev` was missing (Src/BackEnd/Proxy/CMakeLists.txt:83 `find_package(ZLIB REQUIRED)` on Linux, since Qt's Linux build has no ZlibPrivate); (4) `libfontconfig1-dev`/`libfreetype-dev`/`libdbus-1-dev` (+ runtime counterparts) were missing -- libQt6Gui.so/libQt6DBus.so need them at link and load time; (5) FrontEndGUI (Src/FrontEnd/GUI, a `qt_add_qml_module` target -- the one SHARED lib in an otherwise all-STATIC Src/ tree) was never copied into the runtime image at all, so NullockApp couldn't even start -- switched the build stage to `cmake --install --component Runtime` to reuse the project's own existing install(TARGETS FrontEndGUI ...) + INSTALL_RPATH "$ORIGIN" rule (root CMakeLists.txt:89-99, added originally for Linux AppImage packaging) instead of re-solving it ad hoc, which also replaced three separate hand-copies of ui-v2/templates/extensions with the same install prefix; (6) the runtime image was also missing most of the GLVND OpenGL dispatch stack (`libopengl0`/`libegl1`/`libgles2`) plus Mesa's actual llvmpipe/swrast software driver (`libgl1-mesa-dri`) -- QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen still needs a working GL context for FrontEndGUI's Qt Quick scene graph, and GitHub's runners have no GPU. Each fix was verified against the specific error the prior push's CI run actually produced, not guessed preemptively (the one exception: the GL-stack fix bundled 3 packages at once given the ~18min-per-round-trip cost, reasoning from the observed GLVND split rather than guessing blind). The sixth push (commit 6f39fea) is the first to come back fully green: both the `docker build` step and the `docker run --rm nullock:ci --help` runtime smoke step show `conclusion: success` on GitHub Actions run 32611161443.
items.evidence: GitHub Actions run 32611161443, job 'build Docker image': `docker build` step conclusion=success (01:46:14-02:01:51, ~15.5min), `runtime smoke (--help, no listeners/token required)` step conclusion=success; Dockerfile (linux_gcc_64 arch, pip-installed cmake, zlib1g-dev/libfontconfig1-dev/libfreetype-dev/libdbus-1-dev in the build stage, `cmake --install build --component Runtime` instead of manual COPY of individual build-tree paths, libopengl0/libegl1/libgles2/libgl1-mesa-dri + libfontconfig1/libfreetype6/libdbus-1-3 in the runtime stage); root CMakeLists.txt:89-99 (the pre-existing install(TARGETS FrontEndGUI ...) + INSTALL_RPATH "$ORIGIN" rule this wave's fix reuses rather than re-solving); Src/BackEnd/Proxy/CMakeLists.txt:79-85 (the Qt6::ZlibPrivate-unavailable-on-Linux fallback that needs system zlib); no registry push step anywhere in the repo's workflows (grep for `docker push`/`docker/build-push-action` across `.github/workflows/` is empty) -- no published image exists; Dockerfile:22,79 `FROM ubuntu:22.04` still tag-pinned, not digest-pinned.

reconciled.note: Confirmed last wave's build-docker CI job had actually failed on its first real run (never checked before), then root-caused and fixed five distinct real bugs across five CI round-trips (Qt6.7 aqtinstall arch rename, apt cmake too old, missing zlib1g-dev, missing fontconfig/freetype/dbus dev+runtime libs, FrontEndGUI.so never installed into the runtime image, missing GLVND+Mesa-software-driver GL stack) until the sixth push came back fully green -- both docker build and the --help runtime smoke check now pass on GitHub Actions. No published image and no digest-pinned base remain, honestly unaffected -- this closes the CI-validation gap for real, not just 'wired in and hoped', which is what the state stays 'partial' for.

RepeaterParamsView (ui-v2/tabs.jsx) renders three editable key-value tables -- QUERY (from the request-line target's querystring), BODY (only when Content-Type is exactly application/x-www-form-urlencoded; hidden, not shown empty, otherwise -- editing a JSON/multipart body as flat key-value pairs would corrupt it), and COOKIE (from the Cookie header, split on ';') -- each row addable/removable/editable, only offered when current.kind !== 1 (a held REQUEST; Burp's Params view has no response analogue either). Query and body pairs are url-decoded for display / url-encoded on write (matching those two existing functions' own convention for form pairs); Cookie pairs are deliberately NOT url-encoded, since real cookie tokens routinely carry raw base64 '+'/'/' characters that repeaterUrlDecode's '+' -> space rule would silently corrupt on a round-trip. Content-Length is recomputed on any body-params edit, same as every other Repeater/Intercept text-rewrite path. No backend change -- pure client-side text derivation/rewrite of the already-fetched held-message text, same architecture as the five sibling views.

items.gap: IP SAN emission is now correct for BOTH families: sanEntryForHost returns IP:<addr> for an IPv4 literal (already) AND for an IPv6 literal (new strict isIpv6Literal), and isValidHostForCert now accepts a validated IPv6 (its ':' was previously rejected, so IPv6 targets never reached minting and fell through to a blind tunnel). reconciled.note: FOUNDATION + vetted design shipped; state stays ABSENT (no operator hold capability yet). A 3-engineer + synthesis design review produced a GO, implementation-ready v1 with a structurally-safe boundary: HOLD only UNCOMPRESSED text/binary MESSAGES (rsv1/2/3=0), pass CONTROL frames (ping/pong/close) + COMPRESSED (rsv1) + rsv2/3 through VERBATIM. That boundary makes permessage-deflate window desync IMPOSSIBLE rather than merely guarded -- an rsv1=0 message never touches the per-direction LZ77 sliding window, so editing/dropping/auto-forwarding it is provably orthogonal to deflate state (editing a context-takeover COMPRESSED message would silently oblige re-deflating EVERY later message, so that is a documented v1.5/v2 remainder behind a per-connection VERIFIED no_context_takeover handshake). Full design: invert the relay from forward-then-observe to PARSE-THEN-GATE, buffer un-forwarded frames in a per-direction FIFO inside the relay's own event loop (no new threads, no blocking), resolve by a process-global holdId via the existing frameQueued-style queued bridge, with disarm-flush + shutdown-flush + a leaky-bucket cap for deadlock/walk-away safety; a SEPARATE WsInterceptController (the HTTP blocking-worker model can't drive the async duplex relay) reusing the intercept toggle-pair + InterceptRule schema; /api/ws/intercept/* + wsIntercepted[] snapshot + project.json persistence; 7-step build order. STEP 1 IS DONE + mutation-proven (this commit): the pure shared serializer wsEncodeFrame(opcode,fin,rsv1,payload,mask) (FIN/RSV1 bits, minimal 7/16/64-bit length form, fresh-CSPRNG client->server masking) + wsHoldEligible predicate, in Src/BackEnd/Proxy/ws_encode.cpp (Qt6::Core-only), with WsRepeater::buildFrame now delegating to it (dedup, byte-equivalent -- injection regression green). ws_encode_test 26/26 + 2 mutations (16-bit length boundary; text/binary eligibility). Gauntlet ctest + probe_smoke green. REMAINDER (why still absent): the relay parse-then-gate inversion (step 2), the per-direction gate state machine (step 3), WsInterceptController + queued bridge (step 4), /api/ws/intercept/* + snapshot + persistence (step 5), the GUI WS tab (step 6), and the real-WS-client e2e (step 7) -- plus compressed-message hold behind the verified no_context_takeover renegotiation.

items.feature: Comparer: handles large messages
items.gap: 2000 tokens is ~10-15 KB of words, and only 2000 CHARACTERS in chars mode — most real HTML responses truncate immediately. The cap exists because Compare::diff runs synchronously on the control/GUI thread; the fix is to move it off-thread, not to raise the number.
items.why: Verified, including the honest truncation handling. The cap is real and small.
items.evidence: D:/dev/Nullock/Src/Core/Networking/compare.cpp:14 `constexpr int kMaxTokens = 2000;` with the rationale at :11-13 `// The control handler runs on the GUI thread, so bound the LCS table`. Clipping at :74-75 `if (a.size() > kMaxTokens) { a = a.mid(0, kMaxTokens); res.truncated = true; }`. Honesty guard at :122-125 `// A TRUNCATED diff compared only the clipped prefix, so it must NEVER assert identit

reconciled.note: PROGRESS (stays partial). The flat 2000-token/side cap is replaced by an adaptive AREA budget (pure, mutation-proven Compare::budgetedSizes; kMaxCells = 16M = the same ~64 MB / ~100 ms the old 2000x2000 table cost). A side that already fits is kept WHOLE and only an oversized side is clipped, so the common short-vs-long case -- a one-line injected value vs a 30 KB response -- now diffs the long side in FULL instead of clipping it to 2000; two moderately large messages compare at up to ~4000 tokens each (2x the old linear ceiling). The tokeniser's per-side stop rose 2000 -> 20000. The proven O(n*m) LCS + exact backtrack are UNCHANGED (identical output for existing inputs; compare_test green). Verified: compare_test 38/38 incl. new budget cases + 2 mutations (preserve-short-side; both-large sqrt-of-budget); an asymmetric short-vs-3000-token compare is now NOT truncated and diffs all 3000. Gauntlet ctest 98/98 + probe 156. REMAINDER (why still partial, matching the gap's own point): a truly huge SYMMETRIC compare still clips at ~4000/side because the diff runs synchronously on the request thread -- lifting that ceiling needs it moved OFF-thread plus a linear-space LCS (Hirschberg) to raise the memory bound. This narrows the gap for the asymmetric + moderately-large cases without that larger refactor.

items.gap: Query-string parameter names only -- request bodies aren't held client-side, so form/JSON body parameter names never appear in the unique-parameter list or an entry point's params column, a real gap vs. Burp's whole-body-aware analyzer.
